issues.legal_issue: An intra-court appeal lies from an interlocutory order that determines a significant issue affecting a party’s valuable rights and causes serious prejudice.
material_facts: A single judge allowed a proposed assignee to be added as a plaintiff in a pending specific-performance suit, based on an alleged assignment.
The impleadment request was made many years after the suit began, and the order was found to prejudice the defendant by affecting valuable rights of defence.
issues.conclusion: The order was a judgment within the meaning of Clause 15 of the Letters Patent, so the intra-court appeal was maintainable.
issues.legal_principle: Under Clause 15 of the Letters Patent, an order is a judgment when it affects the merits of the dispute or valuable rights of a party; an interlocutory order that determines a matter of moment and works serious injustice may qualify even if it does not terminate the suit. The Court applied Shah Babulal Khimji v. Jayaben D. Kania, (1981) 4 SCC 8.

predicates.intra_court_appeal_from_single_judge_ord: A party brought an intra-court appeal against an order made by a single judge.
predicates.order_allows_late_impleadment: The single judge allowed a proposed assignee to join an ongoing suit after a substantial delay.
predicates.order_affects_valuable_defence_rights: The order affected a defendant’s valuable rights of defence and caused serious prejudice.

issues.definition: When an intra-court appeal challenges a single judge’s order allowing delayed impleadment that affects valuable defence rights, the appeal is maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: An assignee seeking to continue a pending specific-performance suit must obtain the court’s leave within a reasonable time, and leave may be refused when an unexplained delay would prejudice accrued defence rights.
material_facts: A company claimed that it had acquired an interest in a pending specific-performance suit through an assignment made after the suit began.
It applied many years later to be added as a plaintiff and to amend the suit, without filing an application seeking leave to continue the suit.
The delay was unexplained, and the defendant had acquired valuable rights of defence; allowing the request would cause serious prejudice.
The dispute was commercial and the parties were companies.
issues.conclusion: The delayed impleadment request should not have been allowed; the order allowing it was set aside and the application was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Order XXII Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits a person to whom an interest has been assigned during a suit to continue it only with the court’s leave, which must be exercised judicially. In a specific-performance suit, an impleadment application must be made within a reasonable time; an unduly delayed application may be refused, particularly where it would prejudice accrued rights of defence. The Court applied Vidur Impex and Traders Private Limited v. Tosh Apartments Private Limited, (2012) 8 SCC 384. Although amendment powers are broad and delay alone does not require rejection, the serious prejudice and unexplained delay in this commercial dispute warranted refusal.

rule.if: specific_performance_proceeding and assignee_claims_interest_acquired_during_suit and impleadment_request_unreasonably_delayed and delay_unexplained and accrued_defence_rights_prejudiced and leave_to_continue_not_sought

predicates.specific_performance_proceeding: The underlying proceeding is a suit seeking specific performance.
predicates.assignee_claims_interest_acquired_during: A proposed assignee claims an interest assigned to it while the suit was pending.
predicates.impleadment_request_unreasonably_delayed: The proposed assignee applied to join the suit only after an unreasonable period had passed.
predicates.delay_unexplained: The proposed assignee gave no explanation for the delay.
predicates.accrued_defence_rights_prejudiced: Allowing the proposed assignee to join would prejudice defence rights that had accrued to the defendant.
predicates.leave_to_continue_not_sought: The proposed assignee sought to amend the suit and join it without applying for leave to continue the suit.

issues.definition: When a proposed assignee claims an interest acquired during a specific-performance suit, seeks to join after unexplained unreasonable delay, would prejudice accrued defence rights, and has not sought leave to continue the suit, the impleadment request is dismissed.
